messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: Add correlation factors to scatterplot
parts:
Hello,

I'd like to add a text including the corellation factor
into a scatterplot. So far I get the single factors I
want in the text:

r.value <- format(cor(Vs,Vm),digits=2)
p.value <- format(cor.test(Vs,Vm)[3],digits=2)

cor.text <- "Here I want the text"

#and the plot with:

ggplot(data.Vs_Vm, aes(x=Vs,y=Vm))+
geom_point()+
geom_text(aes(0.1,1000,label="test_text"))+
#stat_smooth(method="lm",se=T,colour="black")+
theme_bw()


I want the text as a multiline looking like:

Pearson correlation (Vs ~ Vm):
r = r.value, p = p.value


I think I need to use the substitute function but I don't really understand how to use it correctly. Furthermore I'd like to have "p<=0.001" if it is the case, instead of the real value (like 3.3e-12).

How can I do that?

Best regards,
Johannes

parts:
Hello,

to follow up my last question here a short update:

I manage know to get the text into my ggplot but
I am not really happy with the results.

What I did so far:

#get r and p of correlation
r.value <- format(cor(X1,X2),digits=2)
if(cor.test(X1,X2)[3]<=0.001){p.value<-"<=0.001"}else{p.value<-format(cor.test(X1,X2)[3],digits=2)}

#get text for ggplot
cor.text <- paste("Pearson correlation (X1~X2):","\n","r=",r.value,",","p=",p.value)

and then use in ggplot:
geom_text(aes(0.1,1000,label=cor.text,hjust=0, vjust=0,size=5))

The things I am not happy with:
*) It is not the best way to use the paste() because then I get
spaces where I don't wont them (e.g. in the new line etc, before commas)
*) The "<=" sign doesn't look good, I'd like the "mathematical" proper sign
*) I still don't know the way how this can be done with subsitute which might be the better way instead of paste.

Hopefully someone can help me with that...

Thank you
Johannes

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Add correlation factors to scatterplot
parts:
Firstly, you're rarely if ever going to get a p-value of exactly
0.001, so just use < instead of <=. Secondly, to avoid the = < 0.001
possibility, change r = and p = to r: and p:, respectively. You can
always add spacing in paste() either with the sep = argument or adding
spaces at the end of a text string. If you dearly want the
mathematical <=, then you're going to have to use expression() instead
of paste().

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Add correlation factors to scatterplot
parts:
Hi,

first thank you for your tips...I'll have a look at that.

Now I there is an other problem related to display an equation
on my regression plot. I have several plots with two regressions each.

For my two equations which should be placed in the plot I modified a code snippet from the internet and got following function:

lm_eqn = function(x){
m.Vs <- lm(log(Vs) ~ x, data = move);
m.Vm <- lm(log(Vm) ~ x, data = move);
eq.Vs <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.% italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
list(a = format(coef(m.Vs)[1], digits = 2),
b = format(coef(m.Vs)[2], digits = 2),
r2 = format(summary(m.Vs)$r.squared, digits = 3)));
eq.Vm <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.% italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
list(a = format(coef(m.Vm)[1], digits = 2),
b = format(coef(m.Vm)[2], digits = 2),
r2 = format(summary(m.Vm)$r.squared, digits = 3)));
rbind(as.character(as.expression(eq.Vs)),as.character(as.expression(eq.Vm)));
}


and then I use it in ggplot:

text.time <- lm_eqn(log(TIME))

ggplot(data.time, aes(x=vector.time,y=vector.distance,shape=groupcode))+
geom_point(size=3.5)+
geom_text(aes(0.2,100,label=text.time[1]))+
geom_text(aes(1,10,label=text.time[2])))

I get the equations to ggplot so it seems my function is working. But the result isn't satisfying... there are two problems:

1) The text is the code (italic(y)...) instead of the real text
2) The text isn't displayed nice...it is very blurry and it seems more like
pixcels than a text...

I attached a screenshot that you see what I see. I don't know what is causing the problem?

thank you

johannes

Now I there is an other problem related to display an equation
on my regression plot. I have several plots with two regressions each.

For my two equations which should be placed in the plot I modified a code snippet from the internet and got following function:

lm_eqn = function(x){
       m.Vs <- lm(log(Vs) ~ x, data = move);
       m.Vm <- lm(log(Vm) ~ x, data = move);

                       list(a = format(coef(m.Vs)[1], digits = 2),
                                       b = format(coef(m.Vs)[2], digits = 2),
                                       r2 = format(summary(m.Vs)$r.squared, digits = 3)));
       eq.Vm <- substitute(italic(y) == a + b %.% italic(x)*","~~italic(r)^2~"="~r2,
                       list(a = format(coef(m.Vm)[1], digits = 2),
                                       b = format(coef(m.Vm)[2], digits = 2),
                                       r2 = format(summary(m.Vm)$r.squared, digits = 3)));
       rbind(as.character(as.expression(eq.Vs)),as.character(as.expression(eq.Vm)));
}




and then I use it in ggplot:

text.time <- lm_eqn(log(TIME))

ggplot(data.time, aes(x=vector.time,y=vector.distance,shape=groupcode))+

               geom_text(aes(1,10,label=text.time[2])))

2) The text isn't displayed nice...it is very blurry and it seems more like
pixcels than a text...

I attached a screenshot that you see what I see. I don't know what is causing the problem?

thank you
